beliefs: f strips the first character when the input starts with an uppercase letter followed by a lowercase letter and length ≥3 [E1, E4, E6]
f strips the first character when the input starts with an uppercase letter followed by a digit, space, or symbol and length ≥3 [E2, E6]
f does NOT strip when the first uppercase letter is followed by another uppercase letter, even for length ≥3 (e.g. 'ABc', 'AB1', 'ABC') [E2, E3, E7]
Two-character strings starting with an uppercase letter are returned unchanged regardless of the second char [E3, E4, E7]
Single uppercase letters are returned unchanged [E2, E4]
Strings starting with lowercase, digit, space, or empty are returned unchanged [E1]
Trailing spaces are stripped from every input regardless of first character (e.g. 'a ' -> 'a', '  ' -> '', 'Z  ' -> 'Z') [E8]
The rule is: first strip trailing spaces, then strip the first char iff length ≥3, first char uppercase, and second char is NOT uppercase [E1-E8]
notes: E8 shows trailing spaces are always removed regardless of first character, so I added a trailing-space strip step before the existing uppercase-strip rule. This also explains earlier 'A ' -> 'A' and 'AB ' -> 'AB' cases without needing a space-triggered strip.
